discoveries:
  - (1) The branch head was older than the claim commit, and `gov launch` reads the ticket file from the worktree, so a launch would have been refused.
  - (2) The common brief committed on integrate (DEC-1001 (d)) replaces `flock /tmp/gov-os-rebuild.lock` with `rebuild_slot.sh`. My brief still named the old lock, and the newer rule held.
  - (3) Inside the sandbox, /tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-104 is read-only; only the session's own TMPDIR under it can be written.
  - (4) `gov accept` reads its KPI map only from a table that has a column whose title starts with "Test" or "File".
  - (5) A rebuild can exit 0 with its semantic store not recreated when the shared embedder is overloaded. Retrieval then answers FACET_UNAVAILABLE and the retrieval-regression check shows hit@5 0.0.
  - (6) No role defaults for model or effort exist anywhere yet. The harness uses DEC-839's worker defaults (claude-opus-5-5, high), and `--model` and `--effort` override them.
risks:
  - A verdict is only as good as the judging model's reading of the pass line. Pass lines about "files written" or "the transcript" can only be judged from the session's reply text.
  - `--adopt` runs all three scenarios even when the licence record already rules adoption out, which costs model spend.
  - The harness looks up `claude` on PATH (P-W2-104-CLAUDEPATH).
  - Nothing here fails open: an unreachable model is always not-run, and a missing record is always a refusal.
lessons:
  - Merge w2/integrate before the first launch when the claim commit landed after the branch point.
  - Never set TMPDIR for sandboxed workers.
  - Filter the serial-only entries to the selection, after stripping the tree prefix from select_tests' absolute paths. Otherwise the serial run ends with "no case is named".
  - A heavy slot can take 50–90 minutes to come free; run rebuilds only when no worker needs this tree.
proposed_decisions:
  - **P-W2-104-CMDLIST**, P2, blocks nothing of this ticket's code.
    - Context: DEC-747 needs a new `gov` command recorded in both lists. The tests' list is done (405c3cafa148). `RECORDED_GOV_COMMANDS` in src/gov/check/commands.py is outside the allowed paths.
    - What happened: W1-26's two `[skilleval]` cases are red, and the skill validator flags `gov skilleval` in a code span as an unknown command.
    - Why it matters: those two reds go to the merge queue, and any skill that names the command fails validation.
    - Options:
      - (a) Add the file to W2-104's paths for one line, as DEC-970 did for `accept`. About 5 minutes; then re-run W1-26.
      - (b) W2-120's engineer adds it. This keeps the two reds until then.
      - (c) Excuse the two cases. Not recommended.
    - Recommendation: (a), confidence high. Waiting costs two reds at the merge.
  - **P-W2-104-CLAUDEPATH**, P3, not blocking.
    - Context: the harness runs the `claude` it finds on PATH, while DEC-205 launches workers with `~/.local/bin/claude` because a Windows copy sits on WSL's PATH.
    - Why it matters: real runs only. A wrong binary gives not-run or a real run, never a false pass, so this does not fail open.
    - Options:
      - (a) Keep PATH lookup.
      - (b) Require `$HOME/.local/bin/claude`, with about 30 minutes of test rework.
      - (c) Keep PATH lookup and record it as a residual.
    - Recommendation: (c), confidence medium.
  - **D-1 (lead, P3, recorded)**: the public contract both workers built to:
    - the command and its flags;
    - the `claude`-on-PATH stub protocol;
    - the verdicts pass, fail and not-run;
    - `scenario-records.yaml` beside the skill;
    - exit codes 3, 4, 5 and 6;
    - the `skill-imports.yaml` schema.
    - It sits inside the ticket's scope and changes no KPI. Product-spec may want it written into the spec.
